answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it may earn reputation or receive payments. Spinning up ten thousand fake identities then costs ten thousand stakes, while honest agents recover theirs. Like a willow bending in a flood yet holding its roots, the network survives a swarm of cheap identities because each fake must pay the same price as a real one. A single yarrow stalk is weak, but a bundle bound by stake is hard to break: the vault makes identity expensive, so a Sybil attack scales in cost, not just in count.
